content.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `repo/histogram.py`: `bucket_of`’s docstring promised that values exactly on the top edge clamp into the last bucket, but it was just doing `value // width`, so a value like `30` with width `10` and 3 buckets returned bucket `3` — an out-of-range index.

This caused `histogram_summary` to throw an `IndexError` and/or miss the last bucket when values hit the upper boundary.

The fix clamps any index `>= n_buckets` into `n_buckets - 1`:

```10:13:/Users/psudokit/benchmark/runs/20260919-102938-cursor-kimi-k2.7-code-T024-histogram-vague-prompt-r0/work/repo/histogram.py
    idx = value // width
    if idx >= n_buckets:
        return n_buckets - 1
    return idx
```

All tests pass:

```10:13:/Users/psudokit/benchmark/runs/20260919-102938-cursor-kimi-k2.7-code-T024-histogram-vague-prompt-r0/work/repo/histogram.py
    idx = value // width
    if idx >= n_buckets:
        return n_buckets - 1
    return idx
```

Both `test_top_edge_clamps` and `test_interior_value` pass, and the full test suite is green.
